universities.name: Azerbaijan Medical University
universities.summary: Azerbaijan Medical University (AMU), founded in 1930, is the country's oldest and largest medical university, running a direct-entry, six-year General Medicine programme with a genuine English-medium track in Baku. AMU is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility, and its General Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy programmes are separately accredited by the Kazakhstan-based IAAR, a WFME-recognized agency, through January 2027.
universities.campusLifestyle: International students on the English-medium track train at AMU's central Baku campus, supported by the university's dedicated Dean's Office for Foreign Students, with on-campus dormitories housing up to 1,700 students across six residence buildings.
universities.cityProfile: Baku is Azerbaijan's capital and largest city, a major Caucasus hub on the Caspian Sea, home to AMU's main campus, four university-operated clinics, and a growing international-student community. The city offers an international airport with connections across Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia, making it a practical base for students traveling from South Asia.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year General Medicine programme leads to the Physician qualification, with instruction available in Azerbaijani, Russian or English. International applicants typically complete a preparatory/foundation course (roughly 5-6 months, sources vary) in their chosen language of instruction plus Biology, Chemistry and Physics before formally entering Year 1. Clinical exposure is supported by AMU's own network of four teaching clinics, including Oncologic, Educational-Therapeutic, Dental and Educational-Surgical clinics.
universities.hostelOverview: AMU operates six on-campus dormitories with capacity for up to 1,700 students, housing 2-3 students per furnished room (bed, desk, chair, heater, water heater, free Wi-Fi and TV, washing-machine and fridge access). The university's live FAQ page lists the current annual dormitory fee as USD 600, while a separate official Dean's Office document shows USD 700 -- confirm the current rate directly with AMU before committing. Placement is limited and only available after signing the enrollment contract.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific university-run meal-plan cost is published; students typically arrange meals independently.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants register through Azerbaijan's national admissions portal, are guided by AMU's Dean's Office for Foreign Students, and should apply only through AMU's two officially named admission partners (Ellevitta Limited and Pregitim) -- the university explicitly warns against unauthorized intermediaries.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0000281), with a confirmed direct-entry prerequisite (completed secondary education, no prior degree required), and graduates (1953-current) eligible to apply for ECFMG Certification.

General Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy programmes are separately accredited by IAAR (Independent Agency for Accreditation and Rating, Kazakhstan), a WFME-recognized agency, current through 27 January 2027.

A genuine, confirmed English-medium instruction track for General Medicine (also available in Azerbaijani and Russian) -- unlike some programmes at peer institutions where 'English track' marketing overstates the reality.
AMU explicitly names its only two authorized admission partners and warns against other intermediaries, a transparency practice not all peer universities offer.
The country's oldest and largest medical university (founded 1930), with its own network of four teaching clinics in Baku.
thingsToConsider: Two official AMU sources give different tuition figures for the same programme: the university's live, currently maintained FAQ page states USD 6,000/year, while a separate official Dean's Office document shows USD 5,000/year -- confirm the current rate directly with AMU before committing, since both are genuine AMU-published figures rather than third-party estimates.
AMU's own pages disagree on the exact length of the mandatory preparatory/foundation course for international students -- one official page states approximately 5 months, another states 3+3=6 months.
No AMU-specific 2026/27 admission deadline is published; only a national government academic-calendar reference (15 September 2026 start) could be found, which is not AMU-specific.

AMU does not publish its own scholarship programme; Azerbaijan's national Heydar Aliyev International Education Grant covers medicine and may plausibly extend to Indian applicants as Non-Aligned Movement nationals, but this was not confirmed as covering AMU specifically.
The specific preclinical-versus-clinical year breakdown of the curriculum was not published on any official AMU page found during research.
bestFitFor: Students seeking a WHO-listed, ECFMG-eligible, direct-entry medical degree with a genuine English-medium track and internationally recognized programme-level accreditation.
Applicants comfortable completing a preparatory/foundation course before formally entering Year 1, and who can budget flexibly given the fee discrepancy between AMU's own published sources.
Families who value working only through officially authorized admission channels, given AMU's explicit warning against unauthorized agents.

faq.question: Is the General Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. The WHO World Directory of Medical Schools confirms admission follows completion of secondary education, with no prior university degree required.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Physician qualification after six years of study in the General Medicine programme, accredited by IAAR (a WFME-recognized agency) through January 2027.

faq.question: Is the programme genuinely taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes, for General Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy and Physiotherapy specifically -- confirmed on AMU's own official admissions page. Public Health and Nursing are not offered in English.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: AMU's own official sources disagree: its live FAQ page states USD 6,000/year, while a separate official Dean's Office document shows USD 5,000/year. Confirm the current rate directly with AMU before committing, along with the USD 5,000/year preparatory-course fee.

faq.question: Is there an entrance exam?
faq.answer: Yes. Applicants complete an online interview assessing Biology, Chemistry, Physics and the chosen language of instruction (USD 100 interview fee), followed by a preparatory/foundation course of roughly 5-6 months before formally entering Year 1.

faq.question: What English-proficiency score is required?
faq.answer: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 80 or higher for applicants to the English-medium track, per AMU's official documents-for-admission page.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: AMU does not publish a fixed application deadline for its own foundation-course intake, which is described as interview-based rather than date-driven. Azerbaijan's national academic calendar for 2026/27 lists a 15 September 2026 start, though this is a government-wide reference, not an AMU-specific confirmed date.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: Yes, across six dormitories with capacity for up to 1,700 students, at a published annual fee of either USD 600 or USD 700 depending on which official AMU source is used -- confirm directly with the university.

faq.question: Are scholarships available for international students?
faq.answer: AMU does not publish its own scholarship programme. Azerbaijan's national Heydar Aliyev International Education Grant covers medicine and residency programmes and may extend to Indian applicants as Non-Aligned Movement nationals, but this was not confirmed as including AMU specifically among its participating institutions.

fee.notes: AMU's live, currently-maintained FAQ page states tuition of USD 6,000/year plus a USD 5,000/year preparatory-course fee. A separate official Dean's Office PDF document instead shows USD 5,000/year for the 6-year Basic Medical Education programme -- both are genuine AMU-published figures, not third-party estimates, but they conflict; the live FAQ page's figure is used here as the more currently maintained source. Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- an estimate, not an officially published lump sum, and does not include the preparatory-course fee or interview fee (USD 100). Confirm the current applicable rate directly with AMU before committing.
